name: pi-desktop
one_liner: Runs a local-first coding agent as a desktop app with plugins.

text.why: Run a coding agent only in the terminal and everyone ends up with their own settings and plugins. pi-desktop packages it as a desktop app: an Electron surface over a Rust host core and an agent harness, with plugins the user installs. It works local-first, supports MCP, and is published under LGPL-3.0.
text.take: Moves the terminal agent into a desktop with projects, sessions and review together; still an early preview.
build: An internal agent app everyone on the team runs with one setup
A personal plugin set carrying only the features you use

who.situation: reviews diffs and command output on screen, not in a terminal
gives everyone the same agent app and setup
connects Ollama or LM Studio to an agent

start.text: Download the macOS, Windows or Linux build from GitHub Releases
Open Settings → Model configuration and add a provider and credentials
Add a local project folder from the sidebar, then pick Agent, Plan or Goal

caveat: Early preview: APIs, extension interfaces and behaviour may still change
macOS builds are unsigned by default; first launch may need a quarantine step
Linux needs glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04 and later)

license.scope_text: Link to it freely. Release source for LGPL parts you change.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.
